title: Currency & quantity normalization — personal journal
content:
Quick objective: capture heuristics and sample labels for how we normalize currency and numeric quantities during annotation. This is a working scratchpad — rough thoughts, examples, and unresolved questions.

Notes to self:
- Focus scope on short tokens that appear in UI text and invoices, not scientific notation in logs.
- Two outputs we care about: (1) a human-readable canonical string for downstream models, (2) normalized numeric float + currency tag for analytics.
- Locale quirks: comma as decimal ("3,5") vs comma as thousands separator ("1,234"); context matters.

Normalization target (proposal):
- canonical: "<CURRENCY> <value as plain number> <unit?>" e.g. "USD 1200" or "EUR 1.2M"
- numeric: decimal float in base units (no suffix magnitudes) e.g. "1.2e6" for 1.2M (stored as string for model)

Heuristics (working):
1) Currency detection fallback order: ISO code (USD/EUR/GBP), symbol ($€£¥), currency name (dollars, euros), implied by context (invoice header).
2) Suffix multipliers: k,K => *1e3; m,M => *1e6; b,B => *1e9. If suffix attached to currency code ("USD5k") handle similarly.
3) Locale decimal/thousand: if token contains both dot and comma, decide by last separator ("1.234,56" -> 1234.56 for many EU locales). If only comma and token length>4 -> treat comma as thousands sep by default.
4) Ranges: "$5-7" -> label two candidates or canonicalize to "USD 5-7" with note field? For now mark as RANGE and capture endpoints when obvious.
5) Percent vs per-unit: "%" -> PERCENT label. "5%" not a currency. "$5/unit" -> keep as currency + unit: "USD 5 per unit".
6) Ambiguous bare numbers: if preceding token is currency -> currency; if next token is a unit (kg, m, hrs) -> quantity. Otherwise leave unlabeled (NO_CURRENCY) and mark for review.

Examples (raw -> canonical / numeric):
- "$1,200" -> "USD 1200" / "1200.0"
- "€1.2M" -> "EUR 1.2M" / "1200000.0"
- "5k" (no currency) -> "NO_CURRENCY 5000" / "5000.0" (tag as magnitude-only)
- "USD 3.5" -> "USD 3.5" / "3.5"
- "1.234,56 €" -> "EUR 1234.56" / "1234.56"
- "5-7 dollars" -> "USD 5-7" / "RANGE: 5.0-7.0" (flag for downstream aggregator)
- "£0.00" -> "GBP 0.00" / "0.0" (explicit zero should keep currency)
- "approx $2.5k" -> "USD 2500" / "2500.0" (strip fuzzy tokens but keep note)
- "€1,2M in revenue" -> "EUR 1200000" / "1200000.0"
- "50%" -> "PERCENT 50" / "0.5" (separate label, not currency)

Edge cases to discuss: 
- Parentheses: "(USD 5k)" -> same as plain.
- Negative amounts: "-€3.4" -> capture sign: "EUR -3.4" / "-3.4".
- Embedded text: "about five thousand" -> convert words to numbers when high confidence (use number-parser downstream).
- Abbreviated contexts: "Net + VAT 1.2k" -> separate tokens; VAT handling should not be conflated as currency unit.
- Currency names vs unit collision: "pound" used as weight vs currency -> use context window +/-3 tokens.

Regex sketch (very rough):
- currency_sym = r"(?i)(?:\$|€|£|¥)"
- iso_code = r"(?i)(?:USD|EUR|GBP|JPY|AUD)"
- number = r"[0-9]{1,3}(?:[.,][0-9]{3})*(?:[.,][0-9]+)?|[0-9]+(?:[.,][0-9]+)?"
- suffix = r"[kKmMbB]?"
- combined = rf"(?P<cur>{iso_code}|{currency_sym})\s*{number}{suffix}"
Note: will need to post-process separators to resolve locale.

Open questions / TODOs: 
- How to label ambiguous ranges in single token vs multi-token ("5–7k" vs "between 5 and 7k")? Decide schema for RANGE vs multiple labels.
- Word-to-number conversion reliability threshold — where do we call automated vs human review?
- Should we split currency detection vs numeric normalization as two annotation passes? (Probably yes).
- Add tests for noisy OCR outputs: "$l,2oo" (L instead of 1, o instead of 0). Heuristics: fuzzy char mapping for OCR.

Quick plan for next steps: 
- Draft a short annotation guide (one page) with 20 canonical examples and borderline cases.
- Build a small regex + postprocess script in Python and run on 2K sample lines from invoices to measure false positives/negatives.
- Sync with Tomás re: JIRA-MLABEL-342 to align schema used by analytics.

Notes for reviewer: this is intentionally messy — want to capture heuristics before formalizing. Keep this as a personal notebook until we finalize and push to CONFLUENCE-2456.
